newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses climb sharply, boosted by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses climb sharply, boosted by Wall St.

text.p: European bourses climbed sharply on Tuesday, fired by an overnight rebound on Wall Street that wiped out "grey Friday's" heavy losses.

The dollar was steady against the mark and yen, buoyed by the New York stock market's recovery after turmoil sparked by comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan about the "irrational exuberance" of the markets.
The strongest performer was Frankfurt, which shot up 1.25 percent in floor trading as investors cheered Wall Street's rally and a firmer dollar. The Dow finished some 82 points up on Monday.
"The market factors are all there," said one dealer, "I think we are back on track."
The DAX index reached 2,893.30 points at one point, again approaching the 2,914.61 record it achieved only a day before global market jitters last Friday forced it down four percent.

Many dealers are hoping for a resumption of the traditional pre-Christmas rally on the stock market, and believe that if the DAX can regain the 2,900 point-level it will trigger fresh buying interest.
"If we hit 2,900, then we will be chasing 3,000," another dealer said.

Early advancers included carmaker Volkswagen AG, up after its chief executive Ferdinand Piech appeared to take a more conciliatory note in the company's feud with General Motors, by expressing his regret over the cost and trouble it had caused.

Europe's robust performance came after rallies in Asian stock markets where investors, in the second straight day of share price gains, read the Dow's rise as a sign that U.S. markets had shrugged off Greenspan's negative comments.

In London, the FTSE index rose 0.65 percent with investors stunned by the rapid turnaround in sentiment. At one point on Friday, slumping shares wiped 25 billion pounds ($41 billion) off the market's value.

Though investors drew comfort from Wall Street and a steady bond market, trading was thin. The market was cautious about chasing prices too high after last week's losses, which slowed bull runs on both sides of the Atlantic.
"We have seen a bit of buying of some of the quality stocks but it's been quite selective," one senior trader said.
"A lot of people still expect Wall Street to come off and aren't too keen to get caught with a lot of stock."
In Paris, French stocks rose more 0.5 percent, extending their rebound after Friday's fright and with traders expecting the market to resume its advance.
On currency markets, the dollar was firmer in early trade, helped by Wall Street and Swiss franc losses following confirmation of a weak Swiss economy in the third quarter.
The Swiss franc eyed 1996 lows at 1.3330 per dollar and set fresh 30-month lows against the mark. It recovered to 1.3269 later.

Swiss gross domestic product dropped an annualised 0.7 percent in the third quarter, while the Swiss Commission for Economic Policy forecast growth of just 0.5 percent for all of 1997. The figures underlined recent statements from the Swiss National Bank that monetary policy will remain loose, keeping the Swiss franc under pressure, analysts said.

"The dollar has made a solid bounce back from last week, having blown some of the froth off the markets on Friday, and many of the prior themes will now resume, especially the weak mark and Swiss franc trends," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.31 yen and 1.5544 marks against 113.26 yen and 1.5556 marks in late Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares were 26.2 points higher at 4,037.8
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 11.58 at 2,267.42.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 33.90 at 2,891.14
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $368.90 an ounce, compared to Monday's close of $368.95. Silver was at $4.81, up two cents.
